claims.text: Keep testing limited; extensive lab work is usually unproductive.
claims.quote: Extensive laboratory testing is usually nonproductive.

claims.text: Screening labs: CBC with differential, ESR, BUN, creatinine and electrolytes.
claims.quote: Complete blood count with differential Erythrocyte sedimentation rate Blood urea nitrogen and serum creatinine and electrolyte levels

claims.text: Urinalysis and urine culture, including concentrating and acidifying ability.
claims.quote: Urinalysis (including ability to concentrate and acidify) and culture

claims.text: Stool for pH, reducing substances and fat.
claims.quote: Stool for pH, reducing substances, odor, color, consistency, and fat content

claims.text: Lead, HIV or TB testing depending on local prevalence.
claims.quote: Depending on prevalence of specific disorders in the community, blood lead level, HIV, or tuberculosis testing may be warranted.

claims.text: Review the newborn screen; order a sweat test for recurrent respiratory illness, ravenous appetite, bulky foul stools, hepatomegaly or a family history of cystic fibrosis.
claims.quote: Newborn screening test results should be reviewed for indications of other genetic diseases. Additionally, even though newborn screening tests now assess newborns for cystic fibrosis , a sweat test should be done if the child has a history of recurrent upper or lower respiratory tract disease, a ravenous appetite, foul-smelling bulky stools, hepatomegaly, or a family history of cystic fibrosis.

claims.text: Endocrine: T4 and TSH; IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 when height falls off more than weight, or both fall together.
claims.quote: Testing includes determining levels of thyroxine (T4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH). Growth hormone deficiency screening (done by measuring blood levels of insulin -like growth factor 1 [IGF-1] and IGF binding protein type 3 [IGFBP-3]) is appropriate when growth in height is more severely affected than growth in weight or when height/length and weight fall off simultaneously.

claims.text: Celiac serology (tTG, EMA) can be part of the first evaluation.
claims.quote: Testing for celiac disease may be done as part of the initial evaluation. Testing may include the serologic marker anti-tissue transglutaminase antibody (tTG) and the anti-endomysial antibody (EMA)

claims.text: Imaging only for suspected anatomic or functional causes; bone age if an endocrine cause is suspected.
claims.quote: Radiologic investigation should be reserved for children with history or examination findings suggestive of anatomic or functional pathology (eg, pyloric stenosis, gastroesophageal reflux). However, if an endocrine cause is suspected, bone age is sometimes determined.
